instructions: Finely chop the onion. Grate the carrot and 2 stalks of the celery on the big holes of a box grater, and mince the 3 garlic cloves. Squeeze the 1 lb sausage out of its casings into a bowl.

Heat the 2 tbsp olive oil in a large heavy pot with a lid over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, celery and the 1 tsp fennel seeds. Cook for about 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the vegetables are soft but not browned.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Turn the heat up to medium high and add the sausage. Break it into small pieces with a wooden spoon and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until there's no pink left and it's browning in spots.
Stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, until it turns a shade darker.
Pour in the 1 cup wine and let it bubble for about 2 minutes, scraping the bottom of the pot, until it has cooked down by about half.

Add 1 cup of the broth, the crushed tomatoes, 3 sprigs of the thyme, the 2 bay leaves, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the black pepper. Bring it to a simmer, then turn the heat to low and set the lid on slightly ajar.
Simmer the ragu for 35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes or so. Halfway through, press the sausage with a potato masher a few times so the pieces are finer.
Meanwhile, grate 1 cup of the Parmesan and chop 2 tbsp of the parsley.

When the ragu has about 10 minutes left, make the polenta. Pour 3 cups of the milk and 1 cup cold water into a medium pot. Add the remaining 1 tsp salt and the last 1/4 tsp black pepper, then whisk in the 1 cup polenta.

Set the pot over medium high heat and whisk every minute or so until it comes to a boil, 3 to 5 minutes. Turn the heat to low and cook for about 3 minutes, whisking often, until it's thick and creamy.
Take the polenta off the heat and whisk in 3 tbsp of the butter and 1/2 cup of the grated Parmesan. Put the lid on. If it gets too thick before you serve, whisk in a splash of hot water.
Fish the thyme stems and bay leaves out of the ragu. It should be thick and spoonable. If it's dry, stir in a splash of water. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the polenta into shallow bowls, top it with the ragu and scatter the parsley over. Serve with the remaining 1/2 cup Parmesan and the red pepper flakes on the side.
method_notes: No version that pairs the two had 20 or more ratings, so this leads with RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Italian), whose sausage ragu softens onion, carrot, celery and fennel seed, cooks the sausage meat out of its casings, darkens tomato paste, reduces red wine and simmers it with stock, crushed tomatoes, thyme and bay, mashing the meat finer partway. RecipeTin Eats braises it in the oven for nearly 2 hours and serves it with pappardelle; The Mountain Kitchen browns the sausage first, sweats onion and carrot for 20 minutes, simmers it on the stove with tomato sauce for 30 to 45 minutes and spoons it over polenta finished with Parmesan. This one follows RecipeTin Eats' ragu on the stovetop for 35 minutes, the way The Mountain Kitchen does, over Once Upon a Chef's quick instant polenta cooked in milk and finished with butter and Parmesan.
